messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need to settle the authn/authz refactor before next week's cut. High level proposal: introduce a lightweight 'token-intent' layer so surface API keys are narrow-scope and services get short-lived service tickets derived from them. Thoughts?
kevin: Sounds promising. Main worry is runtime perf — if every request requires a DB lookup to expand intent -> claims we'll add latency.
anya: Could encode 'intent' in a signed JWT claim (compact) so gateway can validate offline. That avoids a KVS on the hot path.
leo: JWTs make revocation hard. If a key is leaked we need a quick kill switch. Suggest short TTLs + ability to revoke via a cache-busting mechanism.
maria: Agreed. Sketch of the payload we were thinking:```json
{
  "key_type": "api_key",
  "scope": "svc:ingest:project-abc",
  "intended_use": "ingest",
  "kid": "k_1234"
}
```Gateway verifies sig + kid mapping, service can optionally re-check via short-lived ticket.
kevin: Implementation question: validate at edge (gateway) or at service? If gateway enforces RBAC per-route we can avoid calls to services, but services doing their own checks gives defense-in-depth.
anya: Proposal: gateway enforces coarse-grained route RBAC and issues an ephemeral service ticket (mTLS or signed short token) for the downstream call. Services perform a lightweight assert for sensitive operations.
security-bot: Note: policy requirement — any widening of scope must emit an 'approval' audit event. Make sure the migration plan includes audit compatibility.
maria: Migration plan idea: compatibility proxy that accepts old long-lived keys and maps them to new token-intent format for a transition window. We can introduce an opt-in enforcement flag per org.
leo: We should also ban new creation of org-wide write keys in hosted accounts. Only enterprise-admins via support flow get temporary broad keys.
kevin: For perf: cache token-id -> resolved claims in gateway with TTL=60s, local in-process LRU, with metrics for miss rate. Cold path hits KVS (Dynamo/Redis) and falls back to verification service.
anya: Also add per-token telemetry (token_id) for anomaly detection and cost-attribution. Keep PII out of logs.
maria: Action items: 1) I will author a short RFC w/ diagrams and threat model; 2) kevin -> prototype gateway cache & cache-busting; 3) anya -> draft JWT vs KVS tradeoffs section + revocation model; 4) leo -> migration playbook and org-policy.
kevin: I'll pick up the prototype.
anya: I'll write the tradeoffs section, include sample revocation sequence.
leo: I'll own the migration runbook and admin policy.
maria: Cool. Please ping @security-team and @infra when you have drafts. Also we should add a small test harness for load: simulate 95th pct latency with cache misses.
deploy-bot: ci/build queued for branch authn-refactor-proto (job 11456) :rocket:
maria: Thanks all — aim to have RFC in 3 working days. :thumbsup:
